Ti4822-xNb samples with a size of 35 mm × 10 mm × 35 mm were produced using an RC-LDM8060 machine (Yuchen Inc., Nanjing, China) with a 2000 W fiber laser and a six-channel powder feeding system. There were obvious black network bands in the samples (as yellow arrows designated), which were regions of segregation caused by the accumulation of Al, also known as S-segregation.

The microstructures of all three samples exhibited S-segregation, with β0 phases dispersed throughout the matrix. As the Nb content increased, the S-segregation became more severe while the amount of the β0 phase decreased.

In addition, the addition of Nb can greatly improve the high-temperature mechanical properties via solid solution strengthening, while also enhancing oxidation resistance.

The mechanical properties of the TiAl alloys depend on two factors. First, Nb is present in a solid solution in the TiAl matrix. This not only alters the phase transformation interval but also strengthens the alloy. The addition of Nb increases the c/a ratio of the γ phase, makes it more anisotropic, and increases the strength of the γ phase [44].
A large amount of Nb in a solution causes lattice distortion in TiAl alloys, leading to stress concentrations.
